q: 1. The diagrammatic representation of the activity of the entire project is called
explain: A network diagram, flow diagram, and control charts are all methods used to represent the various activities and progress of an entire project visually.

q: 2. Construction site planning mainly depends upon the
explain: Effective site planning must account for ground and space conditions, the specific engineering nature of the project, and the required construction methodologies.

q: 3. The pictorial representation of activities and events of a project is known as
explain: In project management, a network (net work) is the specific pictorial representation that shows the relationship between activities and events.

q: 4. Slack time in PERT analysis
options: can never be greater than zero
is always zero for critical activities
can never be less than zero
explain: Critical events have the minimum slack (zero or negative). Per the answer key, d is correct.

q: 5. If the completion time for a particular project is 20 weeks and its earliest expected time is 22 weeks, then the slack time for the project is
explain: Slack = latest allowable time – earliest expected time = 20 – 22 = –2 weeks.

q: 6. Gantt chart indicates
options: balance of work to be done
comparison of actual progress with the scheduled progress
explain: The primary purpose of a Gantt (Bar) chart is to provide a visual comparison between the actual progress of tasks and the original schedule.

q: 7. Which of the following is not a PERT event?
explain: An event is a point in time (start/finish of an activity), not a continuing process. 'Class is being attended' is an ongoing activity, not an instantaneous event.

q: 8. Interfering float is the difference between
explain: Interfering float = total float – free float.

q: 9. In a bar chart the length of horizontal lines for activity A and B are 2 cm and 4 cm respectively. Which one is correct about the activity A & B?
options: activity 'B' need more duration for completion
activity 'A' need more duration for completion
completion time for activities 'A' and 'B' are same
explain: In a bar chart, the length of the horizontal bar represents the duration; therefore, a longer bar (4 cm) indicates a longer time required for completion than a shorter bar (2 cm).

q: 10. Henry Gnatt developed the bar chart technique in
explain: Henry Gantt developed his namesake bar chart technique around 1900 AD to help supervisors see whether they were on schedule.

q: 11. Bar charts are considered suitable for
explain: Bar charts are best suited for minor or simple projects because they lack the ability to show complex interdependencies between hundreds of tasks.

q: 12. The expected project duration in CPM follow
explain: Due to the Central Limit Theorem, the total project completion time in critical path network calculations follows a normal distribution.

q: 13. Which types of network was first developed for planning of any project?
explain: The bar chart was the earliest formal tool used for project planning, predating more complex network methods like CPM and PERT.

q: 14. The relation between jobs of a particular type and various durations they have consumed for completion is expressed by
explain: A frequency distribution curve plots observed activity durations against their occurrence counts to evaluate historical activity variations.

q: 15. Job going ahead of schedule are conveniently shown in
explain: Gantt charts allow managers to shade or mark bars to indicate that progress is ahead of the current date line.

q: 16. The process of calculating the resource requirement of a project is known as
explain: Resource aggregation is the specific technique of summing up resource requirements period-wise across all activities of a project.

q: 17. The upper portion of horizontal bars in a bar chart indicates
options: total duration for completion of an activity
progress of work in the specified time
due duration for the completion of an activity
explain: In specialized bar charts, the upper portion of the bar is often used to shade or hatch the actual progress made relative to the total scheduled duration.

q: 18. Gantt/Bar chart is drawn for
explain: A Gantt chart plots activities on the vertical axis against a time scale on the horizontal axis.

q: 19. The bar chart is also known as
explain: Bar charts were developed by Henry Gantt and are universally known as Gantt charts.

q: 20. The limitations of bar chart are
explain: Bar charts fail to show how activities depend on each other, do not easily account for project uncertainties, and have limited ability to show detailed progress for complex tasks.

q: 21. The weakness in bar charts is
options: uncertainty in duration for various activities
the sequence of activities is not very clear
explain: Because they are simple linear representations, bar charts cannot clearly show the complex sequence or the impact of uncertain durations on the whole project.

q: 22. The prime input of material planning is
explain: Material planning primarily depends on forecasting the demand for materials required over the project duration.

q: 23. Gantt chart is drawn for
explain: This is a reiteration that the fundamental layout of a Gantt chart is activities plotted against a timeline.

q: 24. A milestone chart
options: shows the inter dependence of various jobs
shows the events in chronological, but not in a logical sequence
explain: A milestone chart displays key events in the order they are expected chronologically, without necessarily depicting logical activity dependencies as a network would.

q: 25. A drawn back of bar chart is
options: it is difficult to judge whether an activity is completed or not
all the activities represented are independent of each other
sequence of activities is not clearly defined
it is not possible to judge whether the activity is ahead or behind the schedule
explain: While progress can be marked, the primary structural drawback is that the specific logical sequence and dependencies between activities are not explicitly defined.

q: 26. Milestone charts are developed in
explain: Milestone charts were developed as an improvement over the basic bar chart around 1940 AD.

q: 27. The earliest method used for planning of projects was
explain: The bar chart (Gantt chart), developed in the early 1900s, predates CPM and PERT (developed in the 1950s) as a project planning tool.

q: 28. Mile stones are
explain: A milestone represents a significant event, such as the start or completion (beginning or end) of a group of activities.

q: 29. Actual performance of task is called
explain: An activity represents the actual performance of a task that consumes time and resources.

q: 30. The interrelationship between the functional elements of a programme is achieved through
explain: Work Breakdown Structure (WBS) decomposes a project into smaller components to define the interrelationships of functional elements.

q: 31. An activity is
options: the beginning or end of a specified job
an element of work entailed in the project
the movement of heavy vehicles from one place to another
the progress of work up to a certain limit
explain: An activity is defined as an identifiable element of work within a project that consumes time and resources.

q: 32. CPM means
explain: CPM is a standard acronym for Critical Path Method, used for project scheduling.

q: 33. CPM adopts
explain: Unlike PERT (which is probabilistic), CPM is deterministic because it assumes activity durations are known with certainty.

q: 34. CPM network is
explain: CPM focuses on the activities themselves (tasks), whereas PERT is event-oriented.

q: 35. The optimistic time represents the
options: shortest possible time in which an activity can be completed if everything goes exceptionally well
time in which the activity is normally expected to complete under normal contingencies
time in which an activity will take to complete in case of difficulty
explain: Optimistic time (to) is the minimum time an activity could take assuming ideal conditions with no complications.

q: 36. A CPM family includes
explain: CPM methodology encompasses analysis, plotting, and scheduling techniques collectively.

q: 37. In CPM analysis
explain: CPM relies on activity-on-arrow representation, assumes fixed durations (no uncertainty), and focuses on activity management.

q: 38. Choose the incorrect statement
options: arrow representing activity in CPM network is drawn without any scale
head of an activity represents the finish of an activity
tail of an activity represents the start of an activity
explain: All the statements provided (a, b, and c) are actually correct definitions within CPM networking; therefore, none are incorrect.

q: 39. In the network shown in Fig., the concurrent and preceding activities corresponding to activity 2-4 are respectively
explain: From the given network diagram, activity 2-3 runs concurrently with 2-4 (both starting from node 2), while 1-2 precedes it - matching answer key option b.

q: 40. The occurrence of the starting of an activity is called its
explain: In activity-on-arrow diagrams, the event at the start (tail) of the arrow is the tail event.

q: 41. Dummy activities are use to
explain: Dummy activities (zero duration, shown dotted) are used purely to preserve correct logical dependencies and maintain proper network sequencing.

q: 42. Jobs going ahead of schedule are conveniently shown in
explain: By overlaying actual completion bars against planned timeline bars, a Gantt chart clearly displays activities running ahead of schedule.

q: 43. The occurrence of the completion of an activity is called its
explain: The event at the end (pointy head) of the arrow signifies the completion of that activity.

q: 44. The difference between total float and free float is called interferring float which is nothing but the
explain: Interfering float equals the head event slack; it is the part of total float that causes delay in succeeding activities if used.

q: 45. Henry Gantt developed the bar chart technique in
explain: Henry Gantt devised his historical system of project progress charts around 1900–1915.

q: 46. Which operation must complete first?
options: right of the line joining two circles
left of the line joining two circles
explain: In network logic, progress moves from left to right; therefore, activities on the left must be completed before those on the right.

q: 47. Gantt Bar chart is drawn for
explain: A Gantt chart explicitly plots individual activities (vertical axis) against time or duration (horizontal axis).

q: 48. In a network, the activity which neither takes time nor resources is called
explain: A dummy activity (sometimes called redundant/null in specific contexts) is a logical link that uses zero time and zero resources.

q: 49. The maximum number of tail event occurring in a CPM is
explain: A standard project network should have only one single start event (tail event) from which the project begins.

q: 50. The maximum number of head event occurring in a CPM is
explain: Similarly, a project network should converge to exactly one single end event (head event).
